frequency_question: How often does structural friction prevent the implementation of announced unilateral executive trade restrictions?
membership_rule: Includes major unilateral tariff or sanction measures announced by the executive branch requiring interagency rulemaking, statutory review, or facing immediate legal/institutional challenge before the effective date. Excludes routine administrative adjustments or measures successfully negotiated into formal trade agreements prior to the deadline.
coverage_note: 5 major historical instances named; representative of high-stakes executive trade threats.
known_gaps: Does not capture minor agency-level adjustments or threats resolved entirely through secret backchannel diplomacy without public structural friction.
skeleton: Executive trade actions announced with aggressive short timelines divided by those successfully blocked or modified by structural/legal friction before taking effect.
multiplier: 2 misses out of 5 major contested announcements
validity_reason: Statutory frameworks governing trade (like Section 232 or International Emergency Economic Powers Act) remain stable across this timeframe.
